handoff.purpose: Contains accept(), plan(), dispatch() methods with concurrency safety logic and write isolation commentary.

symbols.name: accept
symbols.note: Returns list of Assignment objects after routing tasks through route_and_select. Non-FREE_LANES decisions are bounced with reason 'belongs to the senior crew -> return to Adam'.

symbols.name: plan
symbols.note: Dry run: calls accept() and returns dict with assignments, spawned count, bounced count, and waves (ceil(len(taken)/max_workers)).

symbols.name: dispatch
symbols.note: Orchestrates task execution. Supports dry_run and parallel modes. Contains extensive docstring on concurrency safety and write isolation.

claims.text: Sequential by default (``parallel=False``): each live write is verified by diffing a WHOLE-repo content-hash snapshot around that one run (offload._repo_snapshot), which catches even writes outside --paths -- but two such runs on one repo concurrently would cross-attribute disk_changed.
claims.why: Reference to offload._repo_snapshot is not present in this chunk; cannot verify behavior.
Code shows can_parallel = parallel and not has_writes, and if parallel and not can_parallel it warns about writable attempts running sequentially. So concurrency requires no writes (isolation).
Code sets can_parallel = parallel and not has_writes, meaning only non-write (advisory) tasks can run in parallel.

claims.text: Declared path disjointness is not a security boundary: a writable agent can touch an undeclared repository path, while ``isolate_paths=True`` would observe only its hints and misattribute the result.
claims.why: Code comment in _run_one uses isolate_paths parameter; docstring warning is consistent with code's cautious approach.

claims.text: Writable concurrency stays sequential with whole-repository snapshots until Forge gives every attempt its own workcell/worktree.
claims.why: Code shows has_writes = any(a.mode == 'write' for a in live_tasks) and can_parallel = parallel and not has_writes, so writes force sequential execution.

claims.text: the isolation now EXISTS -- see gate_concurrent_writes() below, which runs each write through daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt (its own worktree, its own hardened patch capture) fanned out concurrently, and daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.promote_candidates(), which lands gated candidates one at a time behind a cross-process lock with cumulative re-gating.
claims.why: References to gate_concurrent_writes(), daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt, and daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.promote_candidates are not present in this chunk; cannot verify existence or behavior.

claims.text: What THAT path returns is not what this one returns, though: a gated PatchArtifact the primary checkout never saw, not a live write already sitting in repo_root's working tree.
claims.why: Reference to PatchArtifact not in this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: dispatch() keeps its existing auto-land contract for a single write (offload() has always auto-landed a sequential one), and does not silently switch write-mode dispatch to the gated-candidate shape -- that is a product decision
claims.why: Code shows dispatch() uses offload() directly for live tasks, not any gated path. The docstring correctly states it does not switch to gated shape.
